We the 92%: An Anthology of Black Women's Voices
We the 92%

Now Available for Pre-Order

Black women wrote
through this. Every word
of it.

Nearly 100 voices. Essays, prayers, open letters, and reflections capturing grief, clarity, exhaustion, faith, resistance, and resolve. Born in the aftermath of the 2024 election, We the 92% is a living archive of civic and spiritual witness, preserved in a 600-copy hardcover first edition.

Released in time for the holidays

January 2025 to Present

The World Changed.
We Answered.

America Events that shaped the moment
We the 92% How we responded
Jan 20, 2025 Administration

New administration inaugurated. Executive orders issued within hours, targeting DEI programs, federal workforce, and immigration policy.

Jan–Feb 2025 DOGE

DOGE established. Mass federal employee terminations begin. Hundreds of thousands placed on administrative leave or fired, disproportionately Black women.

Feb–Mar 2025 Education

DEI offices shuttered across federal agencies. HBCUs and public universities face funding threats. Black studies and ethnic studies programs targeted nationwide.

Apr 2025 Citizenship

Birthright citizenship challenged via executive order. Constitutional scholars warn of the broadest assault on the 14th Amendment since Reconstruction.

May–Jul 2025 Public Health

HHS restructured. Vaccine program funding cut. Medical expertise sidelined. Healthcare providers report rising anxiety in patients, especially children and Black women.

2025–2026 Voting Rights

Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act further weakened. Election administration targeted. Midterm season approaches under conditions of democratic uncertainty.

Nov–Dec 2024 Origin

We the 92% conceived in the aftermath of the 2024 election. Published under Inkwell & Chalkboard LLC. The call goes out: Black women, write your truth.

Early 2025 Submissions

Nearly 100 submissions arrive from across the country: essays, prayers, open letters, reflections. Every genre. Every generation. Every region.

Spring 2025 Media

Featured on Pacifica Radio and SiriusXM Urban View, featuring The Issues with Wilmer Leon and The Karen Hunter Show. National conversation begins.

Summer 2025 Luminaries

Luminary interviews conducted: Rev. Dr. Kelly Brown Douglas, Dr. Thelma Bryant, Dr. Joycelyn Elders, Prof. Martha S. Jones, Elise Bryant, Farai Chideya, Dr. Yolandra Hancock, and others.

Fall 2025 Endorsements

Endorsements from Marita Golden, Gwen McKinney, and Rene Redwood. Support from activist and author Kevin Powell, whose wife also contributed a piece.

Fall 2026 Publication

Hardcover first edition published. 600 U.S.-printed copies with cloth case and dust jacket. Distributed to churches, libraries, and HBCUs, timed for midterm season.

Nearly 100 Voices

The Contributors

Elise Bryant

Elise Bryant

Union Leader · Theater Artist · Movement Elder

Longtime labor organizer, theater artist, and movement elder. Her essay grounds the anthology in labor, resistance, and first principles.

Dr. Thema Bryant

Dr. Thema Bryant

Psychologist · Past President, APA

Clinical psychologist, author, and past president of the American Psychological Association. Dr. Bryant brings psychological depth and spiritual grounding to the question of what Black women are being asked to carry.

Farai Chideya

Farai Chideya

Author · Journalist · Creator of Our Body Politic

Journalist, author, and Afrofuturist who has covered every presidential election since 1996. Creator of Our Body Politic.

Rev. Dr. Kelly Brown Douglas

Rev. Dr. Kelly Brown Douglas

Canon Theologian · Washington National Cathedral

Theologian, author of Stand Your Ground and Resurrection Hope, and Canon Theologian of the Washington National Cathedral. A visionary voice at the intersection of Black theology, womanist thought, and civic life.

Dr. Joycelyn Elders

Dr. Joycelyn Elders

15th U.S. Surgeon General

The first African American and the second woman to serve as U.S. Surgeon General. Dr. Elders's contribution anchors the anthology's commitment to public health, truth-telling, and courageous witness.

Karen Freeman-Wilson

Karen Freeman-Wilson

Attorney · Former Mayor of Gary, Indiana

Attorney, former mayor, and civic leader whose career has centered justice, community, and the particular weight Black women in elected office carry.

Dr. Yolandra Hancock

Dr. Yolandra Hancock

Pediatrician · Public Health Expert · Reiki Master

Double-boarded in Pediatrics and Obesity Medicine, with an MPH from Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School. Known as Dr. Yola, she works at the intersection of clinical medicine, health equity, and community healing.

Prof. Martha S. Jones

Prof. Martha S. Jones

Krieger-Eisenhower Professor · Johns Hopkins University

Legal historian and author of Birthright Citizens, Vanguard, and The Trouble of Color. A leading scholar of Black American citizenship and constitutional rights.

Chigoke Adoma

Chigoke Adoma

Chigoke Adoma is a retired microbiologist, genealogist, and visual storyteller based in Georgia whose work explores memory, ancestry, and social justice. Through essays, family histories, and visual collage, she honors the voices of her ancestors and celebrates the enduring rhythm of hope across generations.

Marchel Alverson

Marchel Alverson

Marchel Alverson is a writer, communications professional, and founder and CEO of Marchel INK Writing & Editing Services LLC, based in Kansas City, Missouri. A four-time fiction novelist, Thorpe Menn Literary Excellence Award nominee, and proud member of Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc., she holds a master's degree in communications and a lifelong commitment to storytelling.

Jennifer Bailey

Jennifer Bailey

Jennifer R. Bailey, a co-founder of Daughters of the Underground, is an agrarian intellectual activist living in Arlington, Virginia. She is an avid history lover and is honored to be part of the quilt of voices who have come together as part of “We the 92%.”

Kiaron Bailey

Kiaron Bailey

Kiaron Bailey is a doctoral student in Applied Sociology and Social Justice at Morgan State University. Her research examines the systemic barriers affecting Black women's economic outcomes and participation in the digital labor economy.

Lisa Bailey-Harper

Lisa Bailey-Harper

Lisa Bailey-Harper is an Ordained Minister of the Gospel at Alfred Street Baptist Church and Owner and CEO of the LBH Group Inc., serving clients across DC, Maryland, and Virginia in real estate and solar solutions. With over 40 years of service across corporate and ministry sectors, she is a devoted servant-leader whose life centers on faith, community, and uplifting those around her.

Uquay Baker

Uquay Baker

Uquay Baker is a first-line supervisor in the energy sector with a background in counseling children and families within the criminal justice system. She is the author of a 2022 children's book about bullying and is passionate about protecting the vulnerable through both her work and her writing.

A. Fay Barber-Dansby

A. Fay Barber-Dansby

A. Fay Barber-Dansby is a community activist and educator living in Anderson, Indiana. Her work centers on advancing humanity and increasing civic engagement through faith, food, the arts, and conversation.

Phylis Barnes

Phylis Barnes

Phyllis Barnes has spent her career in the Indianapolis Public School District, serving as teacher, principal, and district supervisor and never once stopped there. A lifelong advocate for systemic change and a voice for the voiceless, she has worked extensively in her community and continues to mentor both children and adults. Married for fifty years, she is the mother of one and grandmother of three. Her roots run deep, and so does her reach.

Chloe Beal

Chloe Beal

Chloe Beal is an Emmy-nominated retired broadcast news producer and journalist whose activism runs as deep as her career. For decades she has volunteered with grassroots organizations focused on getting out the vote, including Win With Black Women in Pennsylvania during the 2024 election cycle and Indivisible's BIPOC Caucus, with whom she continues to organize as the 2026 midterms approach. Her focus, in all things, is uplifting Black women.

Harriett Bennett

Harriett Bennett

Harriett Bennett is a keeper of memory. Her work is rooted in the belief that Black women, past and present, carry an imprint of value, voice, and victory that belongs in the permanent record of HERstory. She writes to honor what was, and to ensure it is never forgotten.

Dr. Carlotta A. Berry

Dr. Carlotta A. Berry

Dr. Carlotta A. Berry is an engineering professor, roboticist, author, and founder of NoireSTEMinist® Educational Consulting, who co-founded Black in Engineering and Black in Robotics to expand diversity and access in STEM. Through open-source educational robots, STEM books, and storytelling, she is committed to empowering historically marginalized communities to become technology creators.

Mae Black

Mae Black

Mae Black is an archivist and poet from Tennessee with a B.A. in English and African-American & Diaspora Studies from Vanderbilt University and an M.A. in Pan-African Studies from the University of Louisville, where she wrote her thesis on Apartheid literature. Her poetry is existentially raw, intellectually charged, and viscerally abstract, blending modernist, existentialist, and confessional traditions. Through a voice both rooted and unmoored, she explores the paradoxes of identity, alienation, and belonging.

Tonya Bradshaw

Tonya Bradshaw

Tonya Bradshaw knows the quiet courage of beginning again. After ending a 35-year relationship, she turned toward prayer, meditation, and writing to mend her shattered heart. In that sacred space of healing, she discovered a profound truth:  letting go is not a loss, but a transformative gift. Her contribution to this anthology emerges from that transformative experience, offering a heartfelt testament to resilience, hope, and the courage to embrace new beginnings.

Kim D. Brandon

Kim D. Brandon

Kim D. Brandon is a poet, artist, activist, and storyteller based in Brooklyn, New York, and founder of the Brooklyn Society Writers group. Her work has appeared in multiple anthologies and journals, and this year her writing centers on the revolutionary power of Black love.

Vick Breedy

Vick Breedy

Vick Breedy is an author, poet, entrepreneur, and self-care advocate whose mission is to inspire others to tap into their Bounce Back Magic when faced with adversity. She channels resilience through her events, books, poetry, and Genetically Resilient apparel line.

Veronica Byers-Harms

Veronica Byers-Harms

Having traveled the world in a former life, Veronica Byers-Harms now lays low in a midwestern suburb working and raising a family while rebelling along the way.

Dr. Edith Caine

Dr. Edith Caine

Dr. Edith Caine is a licensed and ordained minister, psalmist, published author, and corporate trainer with over 30 years of experience developing people and improving processes. Her current release is Generational Curses: Do They Really Exist - Freedom is Yours, and her life's purpose is to help others discover and live into their own.

C. Chekejai

C. Chekejai

C. Chekejai Coley is a writer and educator from Philadelphia, currently based in the Washington, D.C. area. Her work centers Black women’s history, collective consciousness, and intergenerational relationships through writing, research, and OMM: The One Matrix Podcast. Witnessing the Black Woman Follow Train is historically significant to her, a moment of collective alignment and resonance starting with the Underground Railroad and she is committed to documenting it, honoring Black suffragettes, and resisting the ongoing erasure of Black women’s political and cultural contributions.

Janel Cloyd

Janel Cloyd

Janel Cloyd is a poet, writer, teaching artist, and mixed-media artist based in New York. A recipient of the 2024 BRIO literary award and fellowships from VONA, Dream Yard, and the Watering Hole, her work, which explores womanhood, spirituality, and the body, has appeared in African Voices Magazine, Obsidian, Cave Canem, About Place Journal, and numerous other publications.

Karen Colbert

Karen Colbert

Karen A. Colbert is a proud Southern sister, a visual arts educator, and a single momma raising an autistic son. Born and rooted in Dallas, Texas, the Big D, she channels her experiences into art that speaks with intention and purpose. She writes to awaken the spirit and give voice to those who too often go unheard.

Tina Marie Coley

Tina Marie Coley

Tina Marie Coley is a retired Juvenile Probation Officer Supervisor from the Philadelphia Family Court, where she served for twenty-seven years. A Distinguished Toastmaster, memoir writer, and lifelong learner, she holds a Master of Science from Shippensburg University and is passionate about preserving Black history and spending time with her family.

Charlotte Cross

Charlotte Cross

Charlotte Cross is a Notary Signing Agent and Real Estate Broker in Austin, Texas. Her work centers faith, integrity, and service, and she is honored to stand with the 92% of Black women who transform challenge into opportunity and inspiration.

AD

Ama Shawna Day

Ama Shawna Day

Ama Shawna Day is the fourth great-granddaughter of Cooley Cameron, a man enslaved and listed in an 1830s will, who survived to be recorded as a Farmer in the 1870 Census. She writes to restore the traditions of her African ancestors and honor the resilience carried through generations in her family line.

Alexis DeVeaux

Alexis DeVeaux

Alexis De Veaux, PhD, is a Black, queer, gender-expansive feminist whose internationally known work spans multiple genres and five decades. The author of several award-winning books, most notably Warrior Poet, the first biography of Audre Lorde, she is recognized for her lifelong activism and contributions to community-based organizations.

Denise Curry Diggs

Denise Curry Diggs

Denise Curry Diggs is a communication educator raised in southwest Georgia who brings her work into both her professional life and her communities. A devoted family woman and Christian, she is the mother of four adult children and grandmother of five.

Belinda Edwards

Belinda Edwards

Belinda Edwards is a Pushcart Prize-nominated poet from the African diaspora, currently based in Santa Fe, New Mexico. Her work appears in MockingOwl Roost, On the Seawall, SageWoman, and other publications, and she facilitates writing groups using the Amherst Writers and Artists method.

Janis Leslie Evans

Janis Leslie Evans

Janis Leslie Evans is a licensed professional counselor and founder of Evans Counseling & Consultation, PLLC, based in Washington, DC, whose career spans decades of mental health service. A Howard University graduate and published author, her books include Recollections About Race and Poetically Black: Reflections on African American Joy, Sorrow, and Healing.

Angela Greene

Angela Greene

Angela Greene is a writer and media professional with 40 years of experience in radio and print, and the author of "Unnecessary Roughness: The Story of a Mother's Fight for Justice". A member of Black Women in Radio's Distinguished Inaugural 30, her radio career is archived in the Library of Congress. She is currently at work on a documentary and book titled "Legalized Extortion", which tells the story of targeted Black doctors.

Leslie Grover

Leslie Grover

Leslie T. Grover, Ph.D., is a historical fiction writer and researcher whose work explores memory, resistance, and infrapolitics. She is honored and grateful for a space reflecting on inheritance, courage, and the quiet labor of survival.

Daphne Hampton

Daphne Hampton

Daphne DuMariuer Hampton is a passionate architect for people, hailing from Houston, Texas. With a mission to uplift and encourage individuals, she strives to embody the change she wishes to see in the world. Through her enlightening writings, Daphne shares insights and inspiration, guiding others on their journeys toward personal growth and empowerment.

Patricia Hart

Patricia Hart

Patricia Hart is a native New Yorker, born in Brooklyn, raised in Queens, whose life in medicine spans more than five decades. Board certified in Internal Medicine and Nephrology and a Fellow of the American College of Physicians, she served as an attending physician in the Emergency Department at Harlem Hospital for 20 years before building a private practice in Brooklyn that ran for over 35 years. Recently retired, she now tends to her garden, her tennis game, and jewelry making.

Caroline Hill

Caroline Hill

Caroline Hill is a teacher, coach, and innovator rooted in Hampton, Virginia, home of the first Africans in America, who created the 228 Accelerator to spark futures shaped by better relationship builders. She blends hands-on practice with emerging technology and lives in Washington, DC.

Tasha Y. Hill

Tasha Y. Hill

Tasha Y. Hill is a U.S. Army Veteran, federal employee, and early childhood educator with a passion for mental health advocacy, living in Northern Virginia. Her work centers on self-reflection, self-development, and acceptance.

Kamelya Hinson

Kamelya Hinson

Kamelya Hinson is a communications strategist and nonprofit leader with more than 25 years of experience in public health, including over 16 years at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shaping messages that reached millions during national health emergencies. She is the Founder and Executive Director of the Ancestors Dream Initiative and the Founder of Cultivating Visions, a consulting practice supporting leaders in strengthening their voice and protecting their legacy.

Margo Hinton

Margo Hinton

Margo Hinton is a poet, teacher, author, coach, and professor from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

Diane Hunter

Diane Hunter

Diane Hunter is a retired educator and emerging writer of poetry, short stories, and memoir. A Key West Literary Seminar fellow, her work has appeared in the Florida Bards Anthology and she is working toward a children's picture book honoring her brother's love of music. Diane currently resides in Florida.

Rev. Dr. Zina Jacque

Rev. Dr. Zina Jacque

Rev. Zina Jacque, Ph.D., is a transformative leader, sought-after preacher, and President and Board Chair of National Senior Communities—the largest portfolio of not-for-profit Continuing Care Retirement Communities, serving more than 28,000 residents. A graduate of Northwestern, Columbia, and Boston University (Ph.D., Summa Cum Laude), she is called to create spaces where possibilities, passion, and purpose meet.

Sylvia Jimison

Sylvia Jimison

Sylvia Jimison is a retired Community Development Block Monitor and former TRIO Director who spent over 14 years helping small nonprofits secure funding to serve their communities. A National Urban Fellows graduate, she brings decades of public service and grant writing expertise to her work.

Angela Bellamy Johnson

Angela Bellamy Johnson

Angela B. Johnson is a semi-retired business analyst and is recently widowed. A Southern-bred transplant living in the North, she writes of the African American experiences through the voices of her ancestors, especially in these troubling times.

Revonne Johnson

Revonne Johnson

Revonne Johnson is the author of the Dear Black Woman poetry series, a collection dedicated to her late mother that focuses on the unique struggles of Black women. Her poetry has appeared in The Mid-Atlantic Review, and she has also written a memoir, Our Side, Our Truth.

Janis F. Kearney

Janis F. Kearney

Janis F. Kearney is a southern author, writing coach, and former publisher of the Arkansas State Press. In 1995, she became the first-ever Personal Diarist to a President, William J. Clinton, and has since dedicated her work to literary legacy, including founding the Celebrate! Maya Project of Arkansas to honor Dr. Maya Angelou.

Kiana Kelly

Kiana Kelly

Kai is a native New Yorker, who has been telling stories since the age of seven. Self-published author of "Love, Kai" their work explores truth, grief, resilience, and the quiet spaces where humanity reveals itself. Kai is also a contributor to Born Brown All Rights Reserved, LLC, and continues to write with clarity, courage, and an unflinching commitment to lived experience.

Evangeline Lawson

Evangeline Lawson

Evangeline Lawson is a multi-media storyteller based between Southern California and Brooklyn, New York, whose work in writing, photography, and filmmaking preserves and celebrates culture. Her photography and writing have appeared in The Washington Post, The Guardian, and African Voices, and she is co-producer and co-writer of the documentary film When We Free the World.

Adriane Louise

Adriane Louise

Adriane Louise is a university administrator and musician whose work centers on helping people feel seen, heard, and valued.

Felina Martin

Felina Martin

Felina Martin is a mother, serial entrepreneur, artist, fashion designer and author based in Georgia She is the owner of the fashion brand, Pamoja na and co-CEO of be in_ marketing, an event marketing and personal branding company. As a creator, business owner and community leader, she is dedicated to positively influencing inclusion and diversity in underrepresented industries.

Dr. Rihana S. Mason

Dr. Rihana S. Mason

Dr. Rihana S. Mason is a cognitive psychologist, program evaluation expert, and author whose creative writing journey began in elementary school. Her published works include collaborative poetry, devotionals for women, and a lifelong commitment to amplifying voices in education and community.

Rabihah Mateen

Rabihah Mateen

Rabihah Mateen is an international development practitioner and writer based in Washington, DC. A New York native, she is also passionate about crafting and marketing her handcrafted jewelry.

Dr. Adrianna Milton

Dr. Adrianna Milton

Dr. Adrianna Milton is a neuroscience postdoctoral researcher at Dartmouth College, investigating neuronal pathways and spinal cord recovery following their 2023 doctorate from Case Western Reserve University. A Florida native and lifelong scholar, Dr. Milton's work spans over a decade of research on addiction, regeneration, and sensation.

Dr. Natoya Walker Minor

Dr. Natoya Walker Minor

Dr. Natoya Walker Minor is an executive leader with a proven track record across government, corporate, and philanthropic sectors, holding a Doctorate in Executive Leadership and certificates from Georgetown University, Harvard Kennedy School, and Case Western Reserve. She serves in ministry, is a member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., and is a proud alumna of the Cleveland Public Schools.

Sharon Murray

Sharon Murray

Sharon Murray came to the page late and arrived fully. Guided by Toni Morrison's charge to write the story you wish existed, she has spent the last few years giving voice to the short fiction she had been composing in her mind for years. Her stories are written for mature women who live full and colorful lives felt, she says, like a favorite melody. Rooted in English Literature and a deep love of music, she writes with both vocabulary and beat.

K L Newhouse

K L Newhouse

K.L. Newhouse is a Trauma-Informed Mediator, Dispute Resolution Facilitator, and Media Crisis Communications Strategist with an advanced law degree in Dispute Resolution. A practitioner, trainer, speaker, and writer, her work is grounded in the belief that emotional intelligence is a superpower - and that cultivating inside work is what facilitates outside results.

Mali Noel

Mali Noel

Mother, daughter, and creative human. Currently resting…

Charlotte E. Forte - Parnell EdD

Charlotte E. Forte - Parnell EdD

Andrea Walker Patterson

Andrea Walker Patterson

Andrea Walker is a writer based in Sacramento, California. Her work explores ancestral memory, faith, and the sacred power hidden within ordinary lives. She draws on personal history, storytelling, and spiritual symbolism to inform her writing.

Janine E. Payne, MPH

Janine E. Payne, MPH

Janine E. Payne, MPH, is a public health professional, creative and community-centered practitioner rooted in faith, ancestry, and lived experience. Born in Cleveland, Ohio, her career has spanned health communications, federal service, and women's wellness. Her current work centers on wellness, meaningful travel, and creative expression for women 50 and over.

Audrey "Coach Hope" Pearson

Audrey "Coach Hope" Pearson

Audrey "Coach Hope" Pearson is the Founder & CEO of Global Humanity Coaching, a trauma-informed practice supporting individuals and institutions impacted by coercive control, domestic violence, and systemic harm. With over three decades of experience in social services, crisis response, and advocacy, her work centers empowerment, accountability, and sustainable healing.

Jennifer Ann Safara Perry

Jennifer Ann Safara Perry

Jennifer Ann Safara Perry is an author, motivational speaker, educator, and spoken word artist, and the CEO and Founder of Sacred Seeds Enterprises, LLC. She is passionate about uplifting her people through truth, justice, and the wisdom of her Ancestors.

Michelle Petties

Michelle Petties

Michelle Petties is a Food Story coach and emotional eating expert whose award-winning memoir, Leaving Large – The Stories of a Food Addict, explores how memories, emotions, and culture shape our relationship with food. As a speaker and workshop facilitator, she leads experiences that help participants uncover their food truths and reclaim their power.

Alpha Richards

Alpha Richards

A recap of a baby boomer's journey of survival, maintaining and thriving as she serves with love unable to hate.

Morgan K. Robertson

Morgan K. Robertson

Morgan K. Robertson is a Baltimore-based entrepreneur, multi-disciplinary artist, and single mother whose work spans creative expression, financial literacy, and community empowerment for underserved communities. Pursuing both her MBA and JD, her mission is to reclaim the stories, land, and legacies lost through centuries of systemic inequity.

Anya Rose

Anya Rose

Anya Rose is an undergraduate student on the pre-law track at Howard University. She studies Political Science, Economics, and Spanish with an aspiration to serve underserved communities in the field of civil and human rights.

Mia Ruffin

Mia Ruffin

Mia Ruffin is a writer based in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. After the loss of her husband, she found her way back to herself through writing and has been grounded in the practice ever since.

ELle S.

ELle S.

ELle S. is a Northern Virginia–based strategist and advocate who works at the intersection of systems, power, and people. A mother and first-time grassroots organizer in the 2024 election cycle, she writes to honor Black women's labor, ancestral wisdom, and collective care.

Fahima Seck

Fahima Seck

No bio given. Need to get from her.

Nicolle Shavon

Nicolle Shavon

Nicolle Shavon is a justice advocate whose most defining chapter has been fighting for her mother. In facing that adversity head-on, she discovered strengths she didn't know she had, deepened her compassion, and learned what perseverance truly means. For Nicolle, standing up for justice is not just an act, it's a calling.

Evelyn Smith

Evelyn Smith

Evelyn Sullen Smith is passionate about writing and amplifying the voices and experiences of people of color navigating the complexities of corporate America. She is dedicated to fostering greater diversity, equity, and inclusion by sharing impactful stories that inspire change and champion representation in the workplace.

Siedha Stephens

Siedha Stephens

Siedha Stephens is a multifaceted artist who specializes in acrylic, resin and photography. Taking the world by storm with hopes of showing the world how art can heal us all.

Tshaye Llorens Taylor

Tshaye Llorens Taylor

Tshaye Llorens Taylor was born in Chicago, Illinois and currently resides in Washington, DC. Her work across education, religion, theater, and technology is fueled by a lifelong liberation quest guided by the principle of Kujichagulia and a reckoning with what it means to inhabit a Black body born female in America.

Tanchica Terry

Tanchica Terry

Tanchica Terry is an applied anthropologist and public health professional whose career spans federal, nonprofit, and legislative sectors. Her writing explores how resilience, belonging, and legacy intersect in times of transformation, guided by ancestral wisdom, sisterhood, and self-recovery.

Dyna Reed Tutt

Dyna Reed Tutt

Dyna Reed Tutt is a retired registered nurse from Palestine, Texas, with expertise in critical care and education. Committed to community involvement, she was drawn to this project as an opportunity to share powerful stories, foster connection, and affirm that we are not alone on this journey.

J F Waters

J F Waters

J. F. has always been an aspiring writer. After losing her husband, writing has kept her grounded.

Candace Webb

Candace Webb

Candace K. Webb is a writer and advocate dedicated to equity, social justice, and public service. Her work honors the voices of Black women navigating systems that often fail to honor their labor, brilliance, and humanity. She lives in Maryland and works at the intersection of policy and purpose.

Indea Webb

Indea Webb

Indea Webb (affectionately known as "Lady Indea") is a woman of God, a prayer warrior, an advocate, and a humanitarian. A woman of destiny with a calling to help other women turn their ashes into beauty, she believes writing is one of the most potent expressions of healing, rest, reflection, and truth-telling.

Shayla Wilkinson

Shayla Wilkinson

SW writes from the heart of lived experience as a mother, a fighter, a believer, a uniter, and a beautifully flawed human still learning and growing. Her work speaks to the ache of injustice and the strength of survival, blending wisdom, faith, and hope. Through her words, she reminds us that healing is possible, and wholeness is revolutionary.

Dr. Andréa Sunsarey Wilson

Dr. Andréa Sunsarey Wilson

Dr. Andréa Sunsarey Wilson is the Founder of Integrity Consultancy Group and Divinely Gifted Enterprises, with over 25 years of experience empowering individuals and families from underserved communities. She holds a Ph.D. in Educational Policy Studies from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and is a proud member of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated.

Pia Wood

Pia Wood

Pia Wood is a retired New York City attorney and published writer whose post-bench life has been shaped by an avid love of reading and travel. A contributor to this anthology, she believes that We the 92% memorializes Black women's determination to remain engaged in the struggle — even in the face of obstacles placed directly in front of us.
